The follow-up correction pass is complete.

## What changed

**11 files vs frozen v15** (was 9 in v1; two new: `foundation/identity-model.py`, `workflows/workflow-cases.v1.json`), **10 files vs released v1**. Full before/after SHA-256 tables are in `handoff.md` §1 and `handoff.json`; before-images retained for *both* baselines; diffs are `vs-frozen-v15.diff` and `this-turn.diff`.

## The substantive shift from v1

I reproduced root's full-Run probe on my own copy first and got **identical runIds** — all four cases ADMIT. My v1 prose mandated a law the reference admission did not enforce. Root's criticism of my own cross-rung probe is also correct: `unresolved-edge@resolved-binding` uses a *resolved* rung, so it could only exercise the resolved-rung refusal.

So this turn the two MUSTs are fixed **in the admission**, at every boundary a Coverage entry or scope can reach: RC-0 relation-specific ladder membership (producer + retained closure + scope mint + **every retained scope a view names**, so a scope with no Coverage wrapper is covered), and the RC-1 minting law (`attempted=false`, count 0, empty classes) actually enforced. Plus CX-BV5-09: `complete` and `not-attempted` now also require an empty class list.

Measured on full retained Run closures: all 8 defect/valid cases behave correctly; **all 17 registered pairs still admit**; the five resolved rungs, RC-2, RC-3, honest `incomplete`/`partial`, free `stageTerminal` and independent `examinedExhaustive` are each preserved with their own control.

## Two things worth your attention

**The Unicode gate has a real cost.** Making the declared version binding *effective* — the fold now raises a distinct `ReferenceEnvironmentError` (never an `AdmissionError`) rather than folding with whatever data the runtime ships — means this reference derivation refuses to run without UCD 15.0.0 case data. That is a genuine portability restriction. I judged it right over an unenforced determinism claim, and said so in the source.

**Reference Run identities moved** (`4e83d795` → `e7abd2f4` → `ca67ad74`). I didn't want to assert that was benign, so I attributed it: reverting *only* `native-evidence.schemas.v2.json` to its v1 bytes, with every behavioural edit still in place, reproduces the v1 baselines exactly. The whole movement is the digest law — a description edit to a registered schema document moves every `coverage2` — and none of it comes from the admission changes.

## Verification

Three probes (28 + 23 + 39 checks), all green — stated as check rows with an explicit aggregation limit, not a coverage claim. Both probes failed on first run from **probe defects, not design failures**; both attempts and outputs are preserved under `evidence/`. One full checker run on the final bytes in a named disposable copy: native 347/347, foundation pass, workflows pass, security 456/456, integration 365/0.

Assessment says plainly that it was written *after* the corrections, not before, as `CODEX-PUBLIC-NOTE.md` asked. I also corrected three misstatements in my own v1 reporting (schema-file count, the writes-under-output sentence, the control count). No disagreement with any root point — the evidence supports all ten.
